title: 2023 AMC 12B Problem 10
statement: In the \(xy\)-plane, a circle of radius \(4\) with center on the positive \(x\)-axis is tangent to the \(y\)-axis at the origin, and a circle with radius \(10\) with center on the positive \(y\)-axis is tangent to the \(x\)-axis at the origin. What is the slope of the line passing through the two points at which these circles intersect?

solutions.text:
The circles are \((x-4)^2+y^2=16\) and \(x^2+(y-10)^2=100,\) i.e. \(x^2+y^2=8x\) and \(x^2+y^2=20y.\) Subtracting gives \(8x=20y,\) so the intersection points lie on \(y=\tfrac{2}{5}x,\) which has slope \(\tfrac{2}{5}.\)

Thus, the correct answer is E.
hints: Write both circle equations, then subtract to get the line through both intersection points
